text:
sara_fin: Vendor John Doe (contractor, personal services) submitted invoice INV-US-555 but our bank flagged backup withholding at 24% due to missing TIN on file. Vendor emailed asking us to gross-up per contract.
tom_sales: Link to invoice in bill.com: https://app.bill.com/inv/INV-US-555
sara_fin: Facts: invoice amount = $5,000, payment initiated but bank withheld $1,200 (24%). Vendor says contract section 4.1 says customer to gross-up for taxes. They want the extra $1,200 reimbursed.
jane_legal: Can you paste the clause? Also need to know vendor entity type: US sole proprietor or corp? Backup withholding applies to payees lacking TIN or with B-notice status.
sara_fin: Clause: "Customer shall pay all amounts due under this Agreement free and clear of any taxes imposed on Customer, and shall gross-up payments where required by law." Vendor is an individual sole proprietor contracting as John Doe, SSN on W-9 missing.
irs-bot: Automated check: backup withholding rate detected=24% (current federal backup withholding). Trigger conditions: missing/incorrect TIN, IRS notice. Recommended action: request completed Form W-9; do not gross-up statutory backup withholding without express contractual language shifting payee's information compliance risk.
mike_ar: From AP perspective: if bank already withheld $1,200, we can either: (A) pay gross and record a receivable for the withheld portion (risk), (B) pay net and advise vendor to provide W-9 to reclaim via IRS refund process, or (C) pay gross only with CFO/Legal approval and get indemnity.
jane_legal: Clause is ambiguous. It says gross-up for taxes imposed on Customer. Backup withholding is imposed on payer (us) but triggered by vendor's failure to provide TIN. Generally we don't gross-up for payee's failure to provide required tax info. Recommend we ask vendor to submit a completed W-9 within 10 days and instruct them how to request a refund from the IRS for withheld amount.
john_vendor: I sent W-9 this morning but bank already processed payment yesterday. I really need the cashflow. Can Redwood advance the $1,200 and we'll sign an indemnity?
mike_ar: If Legal approves indemnity we can consider an advance. Otherwise policy: no gross-up for backup withholding caused by missing TIN. We can offer a conditional advance that will be recouped if IRS refund not obtained. Need sign-off from Head of Finance.
sara_fin: Operationally i'll pause further payments to this vendor until W-9 is in vendor portal. For this payment i'm not processing a gross-up without Legal/CFO approval.
jane_legal: I'll escalate to CFO with clause and vendor indemnity template. If CFO approves, require signed indemnity + uploaded W-9 + evidence of identity (driver's license copy redacted).
irs-bot: Note: If vendor provides W-9 retroactively and qualifies, IRS refund typically goes to the payee; payer (us) can file Form 945 to report backup withholding remitted, and payee can claim credit. We should capture all remittance receipts if we advanced funds.
mike_ar: Tagging cost center 'Contractor Expenses' and marking bill.com status 'withholding-review'.
tom_sales: pinged vendor to expedite W-9 and sent indemnity template.
sara_fin: thanks all. i'll update this thread once CFO responds. :thumbsup:
